d: Aman is a technology start-up that works with clients to identify and manage their specific financial crime risks, by providing innovative solutions to detect any links to criminality. Our goal is to reduce the global impacts of financial crime. Financial crime is a very real and evolving problem. It has been described as “an issue of international security”. Not only is the scale of illicit activity in the trillions, but the impact on all of our businesses, the economy and society is profound. Our award-winning technology platform helps organisations understand these strategic threats through an ESG and socio-economic lens and protects their customers, staff, suppliers and shareholders from criminal attacks or association. In this way, we are fuelling sustainable change in the public and private sectors.

Aman is a socially responsible business that aims to reduce the impact of financial crime through its day-to-day business, increasing awareness, improving capabilities and driving long term cultural change across the private and public sectors. We are a purpose-driven business and are working to meet the highest standards of verified social and business performance, public transparency and legal accountability to balance profit and purpose.

We are looking for a Financial and Environmental Crime Researcher to join the AMAN Insight team. The successful candidate will work primarily on the Environmental Crimes Financial Toolkit (ECFT), our flagship partnership project with WWF, while also contributing to the wider threat-based research output of the Insight team across a range of financial and environmental crime themes. Candidates will ideally have several years of experience in a research role in either the public or private sector, combined with a practical interest in applying AI tools to research and to basic codebase maintenance. The ECFT is an open-access online platform developed by Themis and WWF and launched at the COP16 nature summit in 2024. It helps financial institutions detect and monitor illicit activity linked to deforestation, land conversion, illegal mining, the illegal wildlife trade and other environmental crimes by setting out red flags, risk indicators and jurisdictional and sectoral guidance that firms can build into client onboarding, ongoing review and risk assessment processes. Environmental crime is the third largest illegal activity globally, worth an estimated US$110–281 billion each year and growing by 5–7% annually, according to INTERPOL. This role will act as the day-to-day research lead on the toolkit: keeping its content current, expanding its coverage, and maintaining and improving the web-based interactive tools that sit within it. It is therefore a genuine mix of research and technical work, and we are looking for someone who is comfortable with both. Alongside the toolkit, our recent Insight projects have included:
Jurisdictional financial crime risk reports covering countries in the Middle East, the wider GCC and West Africa.
White papers on topics like money laundering in the real estate sector or the links between financial crime and climate change.
Podcast interviews with leading journalists about groundbreaking investigations like the Panama Papers or the Wirecard probe.
Global survey programmes engaging financial intelligence units, regulators and financial institutions on environmental crime risk.

Given that the scope of our work is broad, our core emphasis is on excellent research, analysis and writing skills; comfort and curiosity in working with AI tools; a strong work ethic and willingness to learn, develop and get involved with all the company has to offer; as well as on demonstrated engagement with financial crime issues. Given the focus of this role, specific thematic knowledge of environmental crime – illegal logging and deforestation, land conversion, the illegal wildlife trade, illicit mining and illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing – and of how these crimes intersect with the financial system, would be a significant advantage. AMAN is a great organisation to join if you are looking for rewarding, meaningful and intellectually stimulating work. We are a friendly team that thrives on working together, supporting each other, throwing ourselves into new projects, going the extra mile, and celebrating success.

Acting as the day-to-day research lead on the Environmental Crimes Financial Toolkit – maintaining and updating its content in partnership with WWF, and ensuring it reflects the latest typologies, red flags, enforcement action and regulatory developments.

Maintaining, testing and improving the web-based interactive tools within the toolkit with the assistance of AI, including prompt design, quality assurance of model outputs, and working with our technology colleagues on new features and enhancements.
Producing research outputs that feed into the toolkit and the wider partnership, including typology notes, country and sector profiles, red flag indicators and thematic reports.
Supporting engagement with WWF and financial institution users of the toolkit, including through training sessions, webinars and structured user feedback.

Drafting reports for AMAN and Themis clients, drawing on desktop research and, at times, primary data. We have a varied range of Insight clients including government ministries, civil society organisations, financial institutions and technology firms.
Gathering and analysing first-hand data, including via surveys and qualitative research interviews.
Drafting country financial crime risk reports examining financial crime threats as well as legal and regulatory approaches in a range of jurisdictions.
Analysing recent financial and environmental crime news stories and regulatory developments for the AMAN blog and newsletter.
Supporting the curation and scripting of AMAN webinars, podcasts and other research related events.
q: A degree in a social sciences, humanities, environmental or finance-related field.
Previous experience conducting research in a public or private sector context - gathering information, analysing data, drawing conclusions and writing up findings in an engaging style.

Practical experience of using AI tools in a research or product context – for example large language models for research, summarisation, classification or content generation – together with the judgement to assess the reliability of their outputs.
A demonstrable interest in global current affairs, the financial services industry, and the impact of financial and environmental crime on businesses, communities and the planet.
Previous professional experience in a financial or environmental crime-related role is desirable but not necessary.
Outstanding written skills - an ability to write clear, concise and engaging reports and articles in English.

Confidence working with AI tools and an appetite to develop this further, including prompt writing, testing and evaluating outputs, and identifying where automation can improve a research product. Familiarity with data handling or basic scripting (for example Python) would be an advantage but is not essential.
High attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to deliver internal and external presentations and to develop strong relationships with clients and partners.
Strong organisational skills, including an ability to multitask and prioritise to meet deadlines.
The ability to assimilate and analyse information about diverse unfamiliar topics, including under time pressure.
The ability to work both independently and as part of a team, including with colleagues and partners in the UAE and UK.
A can-do attitude and proactive approach.
